headline: Joint latent spaces integrate single-cell, spatial and bulk omics across modalities
label: Multimodal Omics Representation Learning
summary: Deep generative and optimal-transport models now align heterogeneous single-cell and bulk modalities, including unpaired and histology-derived data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned shared representations that map heterogeneous measurements into joint latent spaces, whether through probabilistic generative models, optimal transport, or cross-modal alignment. CytoVI models antibody-based single-cell data, CARA transfers scRNA-seq labels to scATAC-seq via cross-modal Bayesian alignment, and AtlasOT couples fused unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein transport with unpaired scRNA, scATAC or spatial data. RAMP extends rank-preserving alignment to cross-platform single-cell and spatial proteomics. What is new is explicit handling of modality reliability: scURL weights omics per cell, and CMGL estimates per-patient modality confidence via evidential deep learning before fusion. DECIPHER applies disentangled representations to cell-type deconvolution, EpiZoo scales a 2.6B-parameter mixture-of-experts model to about 20.9M cells for cross-species chromatin accessibility, and a two-stage model infers transcriptome from breast cancer histopathology to predict neoadjuvant therapy pCR (pooled AUROC 0.79). Several other items, including CauNagi, TxCyto and SCITRAM, address distinct inference problems rather than this pattern.
